security_audit.summary: Most static findings are benign Helm examples, Markdown formatting, loopback URLs, or local validation script behavior. I found one real semantic issue: the examples include a default PostgreSQL password that could be copied into a deployment.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the changeme value, require a user-supplied secret, or show Kubernetes Secret and external secret manager usage before enabling PostgreSQL.

remediation.issue: Local validation script executes Helm commands
remediation.suggestion: Document that the script should be run only on trusted chart directories, keep all arguments quoted, and avoid adding implicit dependency updates.

semantic_findings.title: Default Database Password in Chart Examples
semantic_findings.description: The chart template and playbook include the PostgreSQL password value changeme. Users could deploy the example dependency with a known default password if they enable PostgreSQL without replacing it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited locations define a concrete PostgreSQL password value rather than a placeholder reference. This is a known weak default credential risk when examples are copied into deployments.

content.user_title: Build Helm Charts for Kubernetes Apps
content.value_statement: Manual Helm chart setup is slow and easy to misconfigure. This skill guides chart structure, values, templates, dependencies, and validation for Kubernetes releases.
actual_capabilities: Guides new Helm chart structure with Chart.yaml, values.yaml, templates, helpers, NOTES, and .helmignore files.
Provides reusable Chart.yaml and values.yaml templates with common dependencies and security settings.
Explains Helm helpers, labels, values schemas, dependency management, and chart repository publishing.
Includes a validation script for linting, rendering, dry-run installs, dependencies, and values.schema.json checks.
Covers multi-environment values files and release workflow examples.
limitations: Does not deploy charts automatically or connect to a Kubernetes cluster by itself.
Example repositories, domains, and passwords must be replaced before production use.
The validation script requires local helm and optional jq tools.
Generated charts still need application-specific templates, values, and security review.

use_cases.title: Start a New Service Chart
use_cases.description: Create a chart layout with metadata, values, templates, helpers, health checks, resources, and security defaults.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform Templates
use_cases.description: Align chart labels, helper templates, dependency patterns, and validation steps across team-owned services.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Packaging
use_cases.description: Review chart dependencies, values schemas, repository publishing steps, and dry-run validation before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Helm chart plan for my Kubernetes web service. Include the required files, key values, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Production Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this Helm chart for dev, staging, and production values. Include resources, probes, ingress, and safe dependency overrides.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Harden
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Helm chart for security defaults, resource limits, probes, labels, values schema coverage, and dependency readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Repository Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Helm chart packaging and repository workflow. Include dependency build, chart packaging, index creation, versioning, and release checks.

output_examples.input: I need a chart for a stateless web API with optional PostgreSQL.
output: A chart scaffold plan with metadata, values, deployment, service, ingress, helpers, and optional dependency sections.
A checklist for probes, resource requests, security context, dependency toggles, and validation commands.

output_examples.input: Review this chart before publishing it to our internal repository.
output: A release readiness review covering chart metadata, dependency lock files, values schema, rendered manifests, and dry-run installation.
A concise list of required fixes before packaging and indexing the chart.

output_examples.input: Create a multi-environment values strategy for one application chart.
output: A values file strategy for shared defaults and environment-specific overrides.
Guidance for avoiding secret values in plain values files and validating each environment before release.

best_practices: Keep reusable defaults in values.yaml and put environment-specific changes in separate values files.
Validate charts with linting, template rendering, dry-run installation, and values schema checks before packaging.
Use Kubernetes Secrets or external secret managers instead of storing passwords in chart values.
anti_patterns: Do not publish charts with example domains, placeholder repositories, or default passwords unchanged.
Do not put application-specific logic into helper templates that should stay reusable.
Do not skip dependency lock files or validation when charts include external dependencies.

faq.question: Can this skill create a complete Helm chart from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides structure, templates, values guidance, dependency examples, and validation steps for a new chart.

faq.question: Does it run Helm commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can provide or explain validation commands, but users decide when to run them locally.

faq.question: Can it help with multi-environment deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers shared defaults, environment-specific values files, and validation for each target environment.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes resource limits, probes, security context settings, network policy examples, and secret handling guidance.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I customize before production use?
faq.answer: Replace placeholder URLs, image names, domains, dependency versions, passwords, and values with approved production settings.
